plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, bidding above or below my true value only risks either winning at a loss or losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $6, I should bid exactly $6 to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I only win when it's profitable (value exceeds price paid) and never overpay.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, so bidding your true value ensures you win whenever the value exceeds the price you'd pay, and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down - truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $28, bidding exactly $28 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever it's profitable and never overpay.
